CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

message.content: Hey there! Please read agents.md, read all files it wants you to, and follow it word for word. TASK: Build a basic training script for a 1M paramater model, it should be hyper effecent, with paramaters. HOW: read plan.md. DATASET: fineweb-edu with quality limit, only do above 4 for the score.  REQUIREMENTS: Must be hyper optimized for my hardware, never bloat ram, it should be hyper fast and effecent, ect...  You will train the model on the highest of high quality fineweb-edu data for 2B tokens and provide the scores. Notes: it will be a huge codebase, use a huge folder tree to house all of the data.  At the end of every training session it shall do the proper benchmark + SLERP implementation. You will test the entire framework end to end and get a output score.  ALso, please edit agents.md to say that whenvever editing the training script to change something, you MUST run a 2B token test per feature. Do not add two things and test, you dont know what did what. All scores will be placed into scores.md, this will keep track of commit ID + what was done + if its being keeped or not + description.  You will **NOT** kill any running processes, but you will work around them smartly, do not assume the GPU will be the same, it may be in use, it may not have a GPU, it could be a 3060, ect... plan for everything by using smart systems that will auto detect stuff and attempt to get the absolute maximum out of whatever hardware it is given. At no point shall you hardcode a batch size, gradient accumulation size, or tokens. You will never cap the max checkpoitns it can have saved at any given time (Like limiting to 80 checkpoints) it shall save everything with no limits. ALl print statements, saving stuff, or logs may not intriupt the training process on whateever device it may be on at the time. (stalling quickly to update a log is not tolerated). At the start of the training run it will pull down the models + scores from https://huggingface.co/spaces/Glint-Research/Tiny-ML-Leaderboard on Effecency and overall, then find out where it places in both of those and should properly log it. At the end when everything is being benchmarked it shall get the score on the benchmark leaderboard (using  the pre cached scores for this training run) and will show every model benchmarked where it places in both sorting modes, then at the end right before SLERP it will show the best one, during benchmarking SLERP combinations it will do the same flow of showing the place it scores at in both sorting modes. It will do this for every slerp iteration. At the end it will show the user the final placing in the leaderboard along with individual benchmark scores. When logging to the terminal, never use emojis, use a tdqm progress bar (that expects to be re-sized and doesnt bug out) and logs every 2k steps (also when it saves). So, the overall flow will be this. python3 train.py [number of tokens in billions, like 12 for 12B] [quality score limiter, 4 default, only get scores that are above this or matchig it for data quality]. Once that is ran it will asses how its going to train, its going to see what it has avalible, benchmark the system (do not save, assume new system and new conditions every time), it will see the best batch size, trainign configs, ect... then it will begin the training, if it encounters an OOM it will auto decreese batch size by five, then resume. THere will be no cap on how many times it can decreese add gradient accumulation to make up for the lost batch size. Once training is completed it will look in checkpoints, auto benchmark for the best possible benchmarking config, then it will benchmark all checkpoints using that optimial config for speed (number of questions used for benchmarks will not change). Use wikitext-2, BLiMP, and ARC-Easy datasets. Once benchmarking is done it will do multiple combimnations of SLERP on multipe checkpoints, then it will loop until there is one checkpoint remaining, OR until all newly created slerp checkpoints are worse than the previous best in all catagorys. It should optimize for increesing all scores, not just one.

1	# Plan: MythosMini Architecture
2	
3	## Core Bets
4	
5	| Technique | Source | Why |
6	|-----------|--------|-----|
7	| Layer sharing | ALBERT (arXiv:1909.11942), MobileLLM (arXiv:2402.14905), Glint community design | 70% fewer parameters than BERT with SOTA; deep-thin baseline at 100M demands every param go to effective depth, not unique blocks |
8	| Recursive depth (looped middle) | Universal Transformers (arXiv:1807.03819), LoopFormer (arXiv:2602.11451), TRM line (arXiv:2510.04871) | One shared block looped 4-8x gives 40+ effective layers at ~12 unique blocks' param cost; test-time compute scaling via variable loop count |
9	| SLERP | Model merging / checkpoint soup (arXiv:2404.05861, mergekit) | Spherical linear interpolation of anneal-branch checkpoints, specialist merges, and cross-run checkpoints — nearly free quality gains for tiny models |
10	| SleepGate | arXiv:2603.14517 (Xie, March 2026) | Biologically-inspired forgetting gate + consolidation for KV cache; eliminates proactive interference that kills small model retrieval accuracy at O(n) → O(log n) |
11	
12	## Architecture Sketch (Phase 1)
13	
14	```
15	Input → Embed(vocab→128→W) → [4× Prelude] → [Shared Block × 4-6 loops] → [4× Coda] → Output
16	                                         ↕
17	                                   Per-loop LoRA rank 8
18	```
19	
20	### Layer sharing: ALBERT-style factorized embeddings + cross-layer tied middle
21	
22	- Factorized embedding: vocab → 128-dim → model width. Frees ~10M params vs. full 32k × 512 embedding at 100M.
23	- Unique prelude (4 layers) and coda (4 layers) handle input/output specialization.
24	- Middle block is a single transformer layer (self-attention + FFN) shared across 4-6 recurrent iterations. LoRA adapters (rank 8, ~16k params each) per iteration so each "virtual layer" can specialize slightly.
25	- Total unique blocks: 9 (4 prelude + 1 shared + 4 coda). Effective depth: 12-14 (4 + 4-6 + 4).
26	
27	### Recursive depth: looped middle with variable iteration count
28	
29	- Shared block receives the previous iteration's hidden state plus a learned iteration embedding.
30	- Training: stochastic iteration count (sample 2-6 per step) so the model learns to use variable depth.
31	- Inference: expose as low/medium/high thinking dial (1/4/8 loops). Harder queries get more loops.
32	- Follows LoopFormer's shortcut modulation: residual connection around the loop skips unnecessary iterations when the state has converged.
33	
34	### SLERP: merge recipes for checkpoint soups and specialist merges
35	
36	- WSD schedule with branched anneals: train trunk on stable LR, then fork multiple short anneal runs on different data mixes (code-heavy, math-heavy, chat-heavy).
37	- SLERP-merge the best 3-5 anneal branches into one model (soup merge).
38	- SLERP-merge with the previous checkpoint at regular intervals during training (exponential moving average variant) for smoother convergence.
39	- SLERP-merge specialist fine-tune branches (reasoning, factual QA, instruction following) when post-training.
40	
41	### SleepGate: KV cache consolidation for long-context and multi-turn
42	
43	- Lightweight forgetting gate (2-layer MLP, ~50k params) on the KV cache during inference.
44	- Activated every N tokens in a "sleep micro-cycle" triggered by entropy spike detection.
45	- Conflict-aware temporal tagger marks stale KV entries (KV pairs that contradicted later inputs).
46	- Consolidation module compresses surviving entries into summary representations, keeping cache size bounded.
47	- Dual-phase training: standard LM loss during wake phase + retrieval accuracy on cache-dependent predictions during sleep phase.
48	- At 100M scale, SleepGate should maintain retrieval accuracy above 95% across long contexts where baseline would drop below 20%.
49	
50	## Implementation Order
51	
52	1. **Phase 1a: Layer sharing foundation** — Factorized embeddings, full unique-layer baseline at 100M (no looping yet). Train a deep-thin reference with all unique layers. Prove the baseline works, measure parameter distribution.
53	2. **Phase 1b: Recursive depth** — Collapse middle layers to one shared block with LoRA per iteration. Match Phase-1a quality at ~60% of the params, then use freed params to add depth (more loops or more unique prelude/coda layers).
54	3. **Phase 1c: SLERP integration** — Wire SLERP into the training loop (WS-D schedule, branch anneals, soup merge). Measure gain vs. single-run best checkpoint.
55	4. **Phase 1d: SleepGate** — Implement the forgetting gate and consolidation module. Prove cache-bound retrieval accuracy matches full-cache baseline, then extend context window.
56	
57	## Benchmark & Checkpoint-SLERP Pipeline (Phase 2)
58	
59	### Background checkpointing
60	- Save optimizer state + model weights every 2k training steps on a background thread (or separate process via `torch.save` with `pickle_protocol=5` + `copy.deepcopy` of state dict).
61	- Zero impact on training step latency — serialize to a temp file, then atomically rename into the checkpoint directory.
62	- Keep last N checkpoints and discard oldest to bound disk usage; never delete the best-per-category checkpoint.
63	
64	### Benchmark suite (three complementary axes)
65	| Benchmark | Domain | Metric | Notes |
66	|-----------|--------|--------|-------|
67	| BLiMP (benchmark of linguistic minimal pairs) | Syntax/morphology (66 subtasks) | Accuracy | Measures grammatical competence; 3-shot, pass@1 |
68	| WikiText-2 | Language modeling | Perplexity (PPL) | Standard LM perplexity; lower is better; prompt-aware |
69	| ARC-Easy | Commonsense QA | Accuracy | Multi-choice reasoning; 5-shot, pass@1 |
70	
71	- Each benchmark runs in a subprocess with a timeout, reading the saved checkpoint from disk.
72	- Results are logged to a `benchmarks/` directory as JSON with step number, timestamp, and per-subtask scores.
73	- A lightweight SQLite DB or JSON registry tracks: checkpoint step, all scores, and which "best" tag it holds (best_blimp, best_wikitext, best_arc).
74	
75	### Best-checkpoint tracking
76	- After every benchmark run, compare against recorded best for each category.
77	- Maintain pointers: `best_blimp.pt`, `best_wikitext.pt`, `best_arc.pt`.
78	- Also keep `best_avg.pt` for the checkpoint with the highest average normalized score across all three (z-score normalize each benchmark by its own running mean/std).
79	
80	### Iterative SLERP merging loop
81	This is a tournament-style evolutionary merge pipeline:
82	
83	1. **Seed population**: All saved checkpoints + the current best-per-category checkpoints (including `best_avg`).
84	2. **Generation 0**: Benchmark every seed checkpoint on all three tasks.
85	3. **SLERP candidates**: For every pair within the top-K (by average score), compute a SLERP merge at a sweep of interpolation parameters (t = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75). Use `torch` linear interpolation (`lerp`) with spherical normalization — if both checkpoints are close in weight space, fall back to linear.
86	   - Skip pairs where both checkpoints share >50% training steps (redundant).
87	4. **Benchmark the SLERP children**: Run the full benchmark suite on every merged checkpoint.
88	5. **Selection**: Keep the top-M (e.g., M = 5-10) merged checkpoints by average score.
89	6. **Repeat**: Go to step 2 with the selected population.
90	7. **Termination**: Stop when:
91	   - The top score has not improved for 3 consecutive generations, OR
92	   - Only 1 checkpoint remains after selection (SLERP of a checkpoint with itself is identity), OR
93	   - A maximum generation count (e.g., 10) is reached.
94	8. **Output**: The single best checkpoint from the final generation is the "champion" — the final merged model.
95	
96	### Optimizer: NAdamW
97	- Use NAdamW (Nesterov-accelerated AdamW) throughout training and all merge-fine-tune stages.
98	- NAdamW combines AdamW's decoupled weight decay with Nesterov momentum, giving faster convergence and better generalization than plain AdamW at small scales.
99	- Defaults: β₁=0.9, β₂=0.999, ε=1e-8, weight_decay=0.01. Tune weight_decay via held-out PPL if needed.
100	
101	### SLERP merging conventions
102	- Standard SLERP formula: `θ = arccos(|w₁·w₂| / (‖w₁‖·‖w₂‖))`, then `w = sin((1-t)θ)/sin(θ) · w₁ + sin(tθ)/sin(θ) · w₂`.
103	- Apply per-parameter (each weight tensor independently), not globally.
104	- Handle sign flips: if cosine similarity < 0 for a given parameter, negate w₂ before merging (aligns basins as in Git Re-Basin, arXiv:2209.04836).
105	- Record the merge tree (parent checkpoints + t value) as metadata for reproducibility.
106	
107	### Projected outcomes
108	- Recipe for extracting ~5-15% quality gain across all three benchmarks without additional training.
109	- A single champion checkpoint that out-performs any individual training checkpoint.
110	- Empirical evidence on whether specialist merges (BLiMP-best × ARC-best) or generalist merges (best_avg × best_avg) produce better all-around models at 100M scale.
111	
112	## Papers to Build On
113	
114	- ALBERT: A Lite BERT (arXiv:1909.11942) — cross-layer parameter sharing + factorized embeddings
115	- MobileLLM (arXiv:2402.14905) — deep-thin architecture wins at sub-billion scale
116	- Universal Transformers (arXiv:1807.03819) — shared recurrent block, adaptive computation time
117	- Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning (arXiv:2502.05171) — recurrent depth at inference
118	- LoopFormer (arXiv:2602.11451) — shortcut modulation for elastic-depth looped transformers
119	- Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model (arXiv:2605.19943) — TRM + stochastic reasoning at tiny scale
120	- SleepGate (arXiv:2603.14517) — forgetting gate + consolidation for KV cache PI resolution
121	- WSD schedule + model souping (arXiv:2403.08540, arXiv:2404.05861) — anneal branches + SLERP merge
122	- Tiny Recursive Reasoning with Mamba-2 Attention Hybrid (arXiv:2602.12078) — recursive + hybrid at tiny scale

### Recursive depth: looped middle with variable iteration count

- Shared block receives the previous iteration's hidden state plus a learned iteration embedding.
- Training: stochastic iteration count (sample 2-6 per step) so the model learns to use variable depth.
- Inference: expose as low/medium/high thinking dial (1/4/8 loops). Harder queries get more loops.
- Follows LoopFormer's shortcut modulation: residual connection around the loop skips unnecessary iterations when the state has converged.

### SLERP: merge recipes for checkpoint soups and specialist merges

- WSD schedule with branched anneals: train trunk on stable LR, then fork multiple short anneal runs on different data mixes (code-heavy, math-heavy, chat-heavy).
- SLERP-merge the best 3-5 anneal branches into one model (soup merge).
- SLERP-merge with the previous checkpoint at regular intervals during training (exponential moving average variant) for smoother convergence.
- SLERP-merge specialist fine-tune branches (reasoning, factual QA, instruction following) when post-training.

### SleepGate: KV cache consolidation for long-context and multi-turn

- Lightweight forgetting gate (2-layer MLP, ~50k params) on the KV cache during inference.
- Activated every N tokens in a "sleep micro-cycle" triggered by entropy spike detection.
- Conflict-aware temporal tagger marks stale KV entries (KV pairs that contradicted later inputs).
- Consolidation module compresses surviving entries into summary representations, keeping cache size bounded.
- Dual-phase training: standard LM loss during wake phase + retrieval accuracy on cache-dependent predictions during sleep phase.
- At 100M scale, SleepGate should maintain retrieval accuracy above 95% across long contexts where baseline would drop below 20%.

## Implementation Order

1. **Phase 1a: Layer sharing foundation** — Factorized embeddings, full unique-layer baseline at 100M (no looping yet). Train a deep-thin reference with all unique layers. Prove the baseline works, measure parameter distribution.
2. **Phase 1b: Recursive depth** — Collapse middle layers to one shared block with LoRA per iteration. Match Phase-1a quality at ~60% of the params, then use freed params to add depth (more loops or more unique prelude/coda layers).
3. **Phase 1c: SLERP integration** — Wire SLERP into the training loop (WS-D schedule, branch anneals, soup merge). Measure gain vs. single-run best checkpoint.
4. **Phase 1d: SleepGate** — Implement the forgetting gate and consolidation module. Prove cache-bound retrieval accuracy matches full-cache baseline, then extend context window.

## Benchmark & Checkpoint-SLERP Pipeline (Phase 2)

### Background checkpointing
- Save optimizer state + model weights every 2k training steps on a background thread (or separate process via `torch.save` with `pickle_protocol=5` + `copy.deepcopy` of state dict).
- Zero impact on training step latency — serialize to a temp file, then atomically rename into the checkpoint directory.
- Keep last N checkpoints and discard oldest to bound disk usage; never delete the best-per-category checkpoint.

### Benchmark suite (three complementary axes)
| Benchmark | Domain | Metric | Notes |
|-----------|--------|--------|-------|
| BLiMP (benchmark of linguistic minimal pairs) | Syntax/morphology (66 subtasks) | Accuracy | Measures grammatical competence; 3-shot, pass@1 |
| WikiText-2 | Language modeling | Perplexity (PPL) | Standard LM perplexity; lower is better; prompt-aware |
| ARC-Easy | Commonsense QA | Accuracy | Multi-choice reasoning; 5-shot, pass@1 |

- Each benchmark runs in a subprocess with a timeout, reading the saved checkpoint from disk.
- Results are logged to a `benchmarks/` directory as JSON with step number, timestamp, and per-subtask scores.
- A lightweight SQLite DB or JSON registry tracks: checkpoint step, all scores, and which "best" tag it holds (best_blimp, best_wikitext, best_arc).

### Best-checkpoint tracking
- After every benchmark run, compare against recorded best for each category.
- Maintain pointers: `best_blimp.pt`, `best_wikitext.pt`, `best_arc.pt`.
- Also keep `best_avg.pt` for the checkpoint with the highest average normalized score across all three (z-score normalize each benchmark by its own running mean/std).

### Iterative SLERP merging loop
This is a tournament-style evolutionary merge pipeline:

1. **Seed population**: All saved checkpoints + the current best-per-category checkpoints (including `best_avg`).
2. **Generation 0**: Benchmark every seed checkpoint on all three tasks.
3. **SLERP candidates**: For every pair within the top-K (by average score), compute a SLERP merge at a sweep of interpolation parameters (t = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75). Use `torch` linear interpolation (`lerp`) with spherical normalization — if both checkpoints are close in weight space, fall back to linear.
   - Skip pairs where both checkpoints share >50% training steps (redundant).
4. **Benchmark the SLERP children**: Run the full benchmark suite on every merged checkpoint.
5. **Selection**: Keep the top-M (e.g., M = 5-10) merged checkpoints by average score.
6. **Repeat**: Go to step 2 with the selected population.
7. **Termination**: Stop when:
   - The top score has not improved for 3 consecutive generations, OR
   - Only 1 checkpoint remains after selection (SLERP of a checkpoint with itself is identity), OR
   - A maximum generation count (e.g., 10) is reached.
8. **Output**: The single best checkpoint from the final generation is the "champion" — the final merged model.

### Optimizer: NAdamW
- Use NAdamW (Nesterov-accelerated AdamW) throughout training and all merge-fine-tune stages.
- NAdamW combines AdamW's decoupled weight decay with Nesterov momentum, giving faster convergence and better generalization than plain AdamW at small scales.
- Defaults: β₁=0.9, β₂=0.999, ε=1e-8, weight_decay=0.01. Tune weight_decay via held-out PPL if needed.

### SLERP merging conventions
- Standard SLERP formula: `θ = arccos(|w₁·w₂| / (‖w₁‖·‖w₂‖))`, then `w = sin((1-t)θ)/sin(θ) · w₁ + sin(tθ)/sin(θ) · w₂`.
- Apply per-parameter (each weight tensor independently), not globally.
- Handle sign flips: if cosine similarity < 0 for a given parameter, negate w₂ before merging (aligns basins as in Git Re-Basin, arXiv:2209.04836).
- Record the merge tree (parent checkpoints + t value) as metadata for reproducibility.

### Projected outcomes
- Recipe for extracting ~5-15% quality gain across all three benchmarks without additional training.
- A single champion checkpoint that out-performs any individual training checkpoint.
- Empirical evidence on whether specialist merges (BLiMP-best × ARC-best) or generalist merges (best_avg × best_avg) produce better all-around models at 100M scale.

## Papers to Build On

- ALBERT: A Lite BERT (arXiv:1909.11942) — cross-layer parameter sharing + factorized embeddings
- MobileLLM (arXiv:2402.14905) — deep-thin architecture wins at sub-billion scale
- Universal Transformers (arXiv:1807.03819) — shared recurrent block, adaptive computation time
- Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning (arXiv:2502.05171) — recurrent depth at inference
- LoopFormer (arXiv:2602.11451) — shortcut modulation for elastic-depth looped transformers
- Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model (arXiv:2605.19943) — TRM + stochastic reasoning at tiny scale
- SleepGate (arXiv:2603.14517) — forgetting gate + consolidation for KV cache PI resolution
- WSD schedule + model souping (arXiv:2403.08540, arXiv:2404.05861) — anneal branches + SLERP merge
- Tiny Recursive Reasoning with Mamba-2 Attention Hybrid (arXiv:2602.12078) — recursive + hybrid at tiny scale

This applies even to one-liners you are sure about. If the isolated test fails, the source tree stays untouched while you iterate in `tests/`, journaling failed attempts.

**E2E on everything.** Every change — however small — gets an end-to-end test that exercises the real entry point with real inputs, plus a real run of the suite (`make test`), with the actual output recorded in the journal. Unit tests are welcome additions, never substitutes. Failing tests mean the task is not done: fix the code, or journal the exact failure state and report it. Never delete, skip, or weaken a test to make it pass.

**Tests are permanent and committed.** Isolated proving tests go in `tests/`, end-to-end suites in `tests/e2e/`. They are regression evidence, not scratch files. Full procedure: `docs/rules/testing.md`.

## Scope Rules

Touch only the files and lines the task requires. Needing to edit `batch.py` is not license to refactor, reformat, or "clean up" `LR.py` or anything else. Before editing a file, check its dependents via the callers/callees in `docs/functions.md`; after editing, the tests prove dependents still work. No drive-by renames, reformatting of untouched code, dependency bumps, or deletions outside the task. If an out-of-scope problem genuinely blocks you, journal it and ask the user before touching it. The `git diff` review in step 8 is where you catch and revert scope creep.

## Process Rules

**Commits:** commit after every small unit that leaves the repo working — many per session, never one big one at the end. Committing is your default behavior; do not wait for the user to ask. Messages are one line, lowercase, plain, stating what changed:

```
fix off-by-one in batch loader
add e2e test for tokenizer round-trip
```

No prefixes, no bullet lists, no bodies, no trailers, no emoji. Never commit a known-broken state without marking it (`wip: parser broken on empty input`) and fixing it in the next commits.

**Dependencies:** exact pins only (`torch==2.9.1`), in `requirements.txt`. Adding one means: pin the version you tested, update `make setup`, journal why it was needed. Prefer the standard library when it does the job. Upgrades are their own explicit task, never a side effect.

**Journal:** `journal.md` is append-only institutional memory. Every entry uses the full template (TL;DR, long description, what worked, what failed, what was kept/discarded, next steps) with absolute timestamps and verbatim error messages. Correct wrong past entries with a new entry referencing the old one, never by editing. Template and example: `docs/rules/journal.md`.

**Doc pruning:** at the end of every response, do a quick pass over `docs/functions.md` — grep-check that functions you touched still exist and have callers, delete dead entries. Seconds, not minutes. Do a full audit of every entry only when the user explicitly asks for a thorough prune. This rule deletes documentation only, never source code.

## Final Checklist

Before declaring any task complete, verify each item. Any failure means the task is not done — fix it or report the exact blocker.

1. `make lint` clean (format, ruff, mypy strict — zero warnings, zero suppressions).
2. `make test` passes, including the new E2E test for this change — actually run, output captured.
3. `make pyaot` clean (no errors, no false positives — pyaot.py was updated if needed).
4. New pieces were proven in `tests/` before integration, and those tests are committed.
5. Makefile and `requirements.txt` current if setup, run, test, or dependencies changed.
6. `git diff` reviewed; every changed line justified by the task.
7. `docs/functions.md` updated for every function added/changed/removed; stale entries pruned.
8. `journal.md` entry written with the full template, including test output and what was kept/discarded.
9. Work committed in small, plain-message commits.
10. The diff contains no placeholders, no comments, no ignore directives.

## [2026-06-09 17:55] — ralph loop runner (ralph.py)

**TL;DR:** Added ralph.py: interactive goal → opencode (deepseek v4 flash, max reasoning) plans mini tasks into ralph/, then a Ralph loop runs one fresh opencode session per task until all checkboxes are done. 10/10 tests pass, lint clean.

**Long description:** Researched the Ralph Wiggum technique (Geoffrey Huntley): a dumb loop that re-feeds the same prompt to a fresh agent session each iteration, with progress living in files and git rather than context. Implemented as ralph.py at repo root. Flow: `python3 ralph.py` → asks "What goal do you want done?" → planning phase calls `opencode run --model opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free` instructing it to write ralph/tasks.md (markdown checkboxes, one mini task per line with description) and ralph/progress.md, retried up to 3 times → loop phase runs up to 500 fresh sessions, each told to complete exactly one unchecked task, mark it [x], and append to ralph/progress.md; emits RALPH_DONE when everything is checked. Termination on zero unchecked boxes (counted by regex) or sentinel + zero. Subprocesses run with no timeout because opencode waits out rate limits itself (commonly ~20 h on the free tier); if the process still dies, output is scanned for rate-limit phrasing and the loop sleeps 10 minutes before retrying. Every session's output logged to ralph/logs/ (git-ignored). Max reasoning configured via project opencode.json: provider.opencode.models.deepseek-v4-flash-free.options.reasoningEffort = "high". Model id verified against `opencode models` on this machine; opencode 1.16.2 installed at ~/.opencode/bin. Helpers proven first in tests/test_ralph_helpers.py (checkbox counting incl. nested/star/capital-X cases, sentinel detection, rate-limit phrasings, prompt contract, model pin). Makefile lint/fix extended to cover ralph.py.

**What worked:** `make lint`: ruff all pass, mypy --strict "Success: no issues found in 6 source files". `make test`: "10 passed in 0.01s". Smoke run: model id correct, sample counting correct, goal embedded in prompt.

**What failed:** First lint run: 5 × E501 line-too-long in ralph.py print statements — fixed by extracting variables. Then mypy func-returns-value at ralph.py:150 (`sys.exit(main())` where main returns None) — fixed by calling main() then sys.exit(0). Earlier in session the loop was being built for minimax m3, but the locally configured providers only expose it via openrouter; user redirected to deepseek v4 flash, which exists on the free opencode zen provider as deepseek-v4-flash-free.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept everything described above. Discarded the minimax-m3 model choice (user correction) and the sys.exit(main()) pattern.

**Open questions / next steps:** ralph.py is untested against a live opencode session end-to-end (a real run costs a full agent session and possibly multi-hour rate waits). First real invocation should use a tiny goal like "verify tests work" and watch ralph/logs/plan_attempt_1.log. "high" is the maximum reasoningEffort opencode accepts for this model.

## [2026-06-09 21:25] — rate limit detection verified live and fixed

**TL;DR:** User's free-tier session limit hit; original design failed to surface it (opencode waits silently). Rewrote run_opencode to stream output with --print-logs and announce rate limits live with the retry-after time. Verified against the real limited session; user confirmed it caught it.

**Long description:** Probed with `opencode run --model opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free "reply with the single word ok"`: zero output, process just waits (killed by 120 s timeout). With `--print-logs --log-level ERROR` the truth appeared on stderr: AI_APICallError, statusCode 429, responseBody type FreeUsageLimitError, message "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.", responseHeaders retry-after ~9995 s (~2.8 h), isRetryable true — opencode retries internally and prints nothing to normal stdout. The original run_opencode used subprocess.run with capture_output, inspecting output only after exit, so a rate-limited ralph run would sit silent for hours with no indication. Rewrite: run_opencode (ralph.py:84) now launches opencode with --print-logs --log-level ERROR via Popen, streams merged stdout+stderr line by line, live-writes ralph/logs/<name>.log (flushed per line), and on the first line matching the rate-limit pattern prints a notice with the retry-after wait in hours. Removed write_log (absorbed into streaming). Extended RATE_LIMIT_PATTERN with RateLimitError and statusCode-429 forms; added extract_retry_after_seconds handling opencode's JSON-escaped header quoting. Added tests using the verbatim captured 429 log line.

**What worked:** `make test`: 12 passed (including test_looks_rate_limited_matches_real_opencode_429_log_line and test_extract_retry_after_seconds_from_real_log_line == 9995). `make lint` clean after `make fix`. Live probe wrote the real 429 line into ralph/logs/limit_detection_probe.log and, after the flush fix, the user confirmed detection: announcement printed as soon as the 429 arrived.

**What failed:** First live probe logged the 429 but printed no announcement — Python block-buffers stdout when piped, and the kill discarded the buffer. Fixed with print(..., flush=True) in announce_rate_limit. Also one ruff format failure on the multiline message (fixed via make fix).

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept streaming run_opencode, flush fix, widened patterns, real-log-line tests. Discarded write_log and the capture-after-exit design. Probe logs left git-ignored in ralph/logs/.

**Open questions / next steps:** handle_failed_iteration still covers only the rare case where opencode exits nonzero; normal limits never reach it since opencode waits internally — fine by design. Current limit clears in roughly 2.8 h from 21:16; a real ralph run can start after that.

## [2026-06-09 22:05] — opencode auto-install/update and freebuff fallback

**TL;DR:** ralph.py now installs/updates opencode at every launch and, after 3 consecutive opencode deaths, falls back to freebuff configured for MiniMax M3 in standard mode. freebuff has no headless CLI, so the fallback is an interactive handoff. 15/15 tests, lint clean, both ensure functions verified live.

**Long description:** Researched freebuff (CodebuffAI, npm `freebuff`, v0.0.105 installed): ad-supported free agent, `freebuff --help` exposes only login/--continue/--cwd — no one-shot prompt, no model flag; piping stdin just renders the TUI. Strings dump of the ~48 MB binary at ~/.config/manicode/freebuff: no headless/--print flags (the lone "-p"/"headless" hits were tokenizer vocab and a bot-UA list), but model ids incl. minimax/minimax-m3 and mode values DEFAULT/LITE/MAX are present, and ~/.config/manicode/settings.json carries {"mode","freebuffModel"} — so model selection is config-file driven; DEFAULT is the standard mode. Implementation in ralph.py: ensure_opencode() (main runs it first) prepends ~/.opencode/bin to PATH, installs via `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash` when missing (SystemExit on failure), else best-effort `opencode upgrade`; merge_freebuff_settings() pure JSON transform forcing freebuffModel=minimax/minimax-m3 + mode=DEFAULT, preserving other keys; ensure_freebuff() npm-installs when missing and writes settings; run_freebuff_fallback() explains the handoff and runs the blocking interactive TUI; ralph_loop tracks consecutive_failures, triggers the fallback at 3, resets after.

**What worked:** `make lint` clean (mypy strict, 6 files), `make test` 15 passed (new: merge settings from empty, merge preserving adsEnabled while overriding model/mode, failure-limit constant). Live: ensure_opencode → "opencode is up to date" (`opencode upgrade` exit 0); ensure_freebuff → settings.json now {"mode":"DEFAULT","adsEnabled":true,"freebuffModel":"minimax/minimax-m3"}.

**What failed:** Nothing in code. Research dead ends recorded so they are not retried: freebuff has no headless invocation (no -p/--print/run subcommand, stdin piping ignored), so a fully automated freebuff fallback is impossible at v0.0.105; interactive handoff is the only option.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept everything above. Discarded the idea of an automated freebuff fallback (no headless mode exists).

**Open questions / next steps:** run_freebuff_fallback assumes a human is at the terminal; in a fully unattended run the TUI would sit idle until exited. If freebuff ever ships a headless mode, swap the handoff for a real automated fallback.

## [2026-06-09 22:30] — freebuff bridge across opencode rate-limit windows

**TL;DR:** Rate limits now trigger an automatic switch: run_opencode kills the session the moment a 429 appears and returns the retry-after; rate_limit_handoff runs freebuff (minimax m3, standard) during the window, sleeps out whatever remains, then the loop returns to opencode. 16/16 tests, lint clean.

**Long description:** Previously a rate-limited opencode session was left running (opencode waits internally, commonly ~20 h). New behavior: run_opencode (ralph.py:83) detects the first rate-limit line, resolves the wait (header retry-after, else DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_SECONDS = 72000 = 20 h), terminates the opencode subprocess, and returns a 3-tuple (returncode, output, retry_after). Both plan_tasks and ralph_loop check retry_after before anything else and call rate_limit_handoff(wait): prints the resume clock time, ensures freebuff is configured, hands the terminal to the interactive freebuff session, and after freebuff exits sleeps the remainder of the window (monotonic deadline), then announces the switch back to opencode since it is faster. Rate-limited iterations do not count toward the consecutive-failure fallback. announce_rate_limit was removed (folded into run_opencode + rate_limit_handoff).

**What worked:** `make lint` clean, `make test` 16 passed (new: DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_SECONDS == 72000). Stubbed simulation of rate_limit_handoff(5) produced the exact sequence: ensure_freebuff → run freebuff → sleep remaining ~5 s → "switching back to opencode".

**What failed:** One E501 (101-char print) on first lint — fixed by extracting wait_hours. The earlier sed-based doc cleanup left two stale announce_rate_limit references inside the run_opencode entry; fixed by rewriting that entry.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept the 3-tuple run_opencode contract and handoff. Discarded announce_rate_limit and the leave-opencode-waiting behavior.

**Open questions / next steps:** The handoff is not yet exercised against a live 429 end-to-end (would burn a real 20 h window); the detection regex and retry-after parsing are covered by tests built from the captured real log line, and the handoff sequencing by the stubbed run. If freebuff itself rate-limits during the window there is no further fallback — the user just exits and ralph sleeps out the rest.

## [2026-06-09 23:10] — smarter verify-loop and live freebuff E2E pass

**TL;DR:** Ralph loop rewritten to execute-then-verify with continuation feedback; freebuff fallback is now fully autonomous via tmux and passed a live end-to-end probe: MiniMax M3 created the probe file and checked off its task, detected by ralph's poller (task completed: True).

**Long description:** Loop redesign per user request: plan goals → worker agent executes the first unchecked task → a separate fresh verifier agent checks it (build_verify_prompt: read AGENTS.md, confirm work exists, run make lint/test; reply RALPH_VERIFIED or uncheck the box, log findings, reply RALPH_INCOMPLETE + remains) → if incomplete, the next worker prompt quotes the verifier findings and says continue from the partial work, do not restart. Worker prompt (build_task_prompt) now explicitly orders reading AGENTS.md completely, journal.md, docs/functions.md, ralph/tasks.md, ralph/progress.md before touching anything. Removed build_loop_prompt/output_signals_done/DONE_SENTINEL (dead). New helpers: first_incomplete_task, verification_feedback (None on verified, else last 1500 chars), verify_task (synthesizes RALPH_INCOMPLETE feedback when the verifier rate-limits or crashes so unverified work is never accepted). Freebuff fallback driving rewritten around tmux: start_freebuff_session waits for the "Enter a coding task" ready marker (no blind sleep), auto-presses Enter on the "Freebuff is already running" take-over dialog; send_prompt_to_freebuff sends the flattened prompt literally (-l), waits 2 s, then sends Enter separately.

Live probe (real freebuff session in tmux, MiniMax M3 · unlimited shown in TUI): prompt injected and submitted, freebuff created ralph/freebuff_probe.txt containing exactly "ok" and flipped the checkbox to [x]; run_freebuff_task's poller saw the unchecked count drop and returned True; session killed cleanly.

(2) Second attempt: "Freebuff is already running" take-over dialog blocked startup; auto-Enter added. (3) Third: text landed in input box but the same-call Enter was swallowed — text visible, never submitted; fixed by separate delayed Enter. Also twice killed my own shell with pkill -f freebuff (pattern matched the running command line) — use tmux kill-session instead, never pkill -f with a word in your own command.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept everything above. Discarded build_loop_prompt, output_signals_done, DONE_SENTINEL, the fixed startup sleep, single-call send-keys. Probe artifacts (ralph/tasks.md, progress.md, freebuff_probe.txt) deleted after the test.

**Open questions / next steps:** Freebuff progress detection is checkbox-based; a freebuff agent that finishes work but forgets to flip the box reads as "no progress". The opencode side's verifier covers that case; freebuff side accepts it as a time-box miss. FREEBUFF_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120, poll 30 s, task box 40 min.

## [2026-06-10 00:05] — re-plan step, resume state, freebuff verification parity

**TL;DR:** Added the three chosen ralph upgrades: periodic re-planning every 5 verified tasks, persistent resume state in ralph/state.json, and verification of freebuff-completed tasks once opencode is back. 24/24 tests, lint clean.

**What failed:** Nothing this unit; first lint/test run was clean.

## [2026-06-10 00:40] — fix planning-phase rate-limit crash in rate_limit_handoff

**TL;DR:** Live run crashed with FileNotFoundError: rate_limit_handoff read ralph/tasks.md unconditionally, but a rate limit during planning means tasks.md does not exist yet. Added unfinished_work_remains guard; 26/26 tests, lint clean.

**Long description:** User ran `python3 ralph.py` with goal "make test.py with a simple script"; the very first planning call hit the 429 (retry-after ~1.5 h). rate_limit_handoff correctly skipped the freebuff leg (TASKS_FILE.is_file() guard at line 326), but the remaining-window check at line 334 called `count_incomplete_tasks(TASKS_FILE.read_text())` with no existence guard → `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/home/lane/MythosMini/ralph/tasks.md'`. Proving tests written first in tests/test_ralph_helpers.py (missing file → True; one unchecked → True; all checked → False) with TASKS_FILE monkeypatched to tmp_path.

**What failed:** Nothing; first run clean.

## [2026-06-10 01:10] — freebuff planning fallback for rate-limited planning phase

AGENTS.md journal rule changed to read the full file. 35/35 tests, lint clean.

**Long description:** User's live run: goal "make a basic file with some content", first planning call hit the 429 (retry-after ~1.5 h), output showed "waiting 1.5 h for the opencode rate limit to clear" with no freebuff use — the `TASKS_FILE.is_file()` guard in rate_limit_handoff existed to prevent freebuff working tasks that don't exist, but it also blocked freebuff from doing anything during a planning-phase limit. E2E tests/e2e/test_planning_rate_limit_handoff.py drives the real plan_tasks through a stubbed 429 into the freebuff planning path and asserts the printed sequence and final tasks.md state. `make lint` clean (ruff format/check, mypy --strict, 7 files). `make test` 35 passed.

## [2026-06-10 01:55] — plan.md with architecture bets: layer sharing, recursive depth, SLERP, SleepGate

**TL;DR:** Created `plan.md` detailing the four core architecture bets for MythosMini: layer sharing (ALBERT-style factorized embeddings + cross-layer tied middle), recursive depth (looped shared block with per-loop LoRA), SLERP (spherical linear interpolation for checkpoint merging), and SleepGate (forgetting gate for KV cache consolidation). 40/40 tests, lint clean.

**Long description:** User requested a plan.md file detailing what we will use. Four techniques specified: layer sharing, recursive depth, SLERP, and SleepGate. Wrote plan.md with:
- Layer sharing section covering ALBERT factorized embeddings (vocab→128→W) and cross-layer parameter sharing for the middle block, informed by research.md idea #22 (ALBERT), #27 (per-layer LoRA on shared block), and community design C1 (Glint's looped-core with LoRA)
- Recursive depth section covering the looped middle block with 4-6 iterations, variable loop count at inference, and LoopFormer-style shortcut modulation — from research.md ideas #22/#23 and papers Universal Transformers, LoopFormer, TRM
- SLERP section covering checkpoint soups, WSD branched anneals, specialist merge recipes — from research.md ideas #49, #70, #98
- SleepGate section based on arXiv:2603.14517 (Xie, March 2026): forgetting gate + conflict-aware temporal tagger + consolidation module for KV cache proactive interference resolution

# Testing Procedure

The codebase is a fancy, expensive PC. `tests/` is the trash PC where every part gets tested before installation. Nothing unproven touches the expensive machine.

## Layout

- `tests/` — isolated proving tests: each new function, dependency, or algorithm demonstrated working on its own with real inputs and real assertions.
- `tests/e2e/` — end-to-end suites: exercise the real entry point (the actual script/CLI/pipeline), not isolated functions.
- All tests are committed. They are permanent regression evidence, never scratch files to delete after use.
- Test files follow pytest conventions: `test_<subject>.py`, functions named `test_<behavior>`.

## Sandbox-first workflow

1. Write the proving test in `tests/` for the new piece, with real inputs and assertions on real outputs — no mocked-away core behavior, no placeholder fixtures.
2. Run it against the isolated implementation: `python -m pytest tests/test_<subject>.py -v`.
3. If it fails: iterate in `tests/` only — the source tree stays untouched. Journal each failed attempt with the verbatim error so it is never retried blindly.
4. Once it passes: integrate the piece into the codebase proper.
5. Run the full suite (`make test`) to confirm nothing else broke.

This applies to everything, including "obviously correct" one-liners and library calls you are sure about — those are exactly the parts that brick expensive PCs.

## E2E requirements

- Every change gets an e2e test, however small the change. A one-line fix still gets a run proving the fix at the real entry point.
- "E2E" means running the actual entry point with real inputs and asserting on real outputs. Unit tests are welcome additions, never substitutes.
- Run the tests; do not just write them. Capture the actual command and output in the journal entry (pass/fail counts, verbatim failure output).
- A failing test means the task is not done. Fix the code until it passes, or journal the exact failure state and report it to the user. Never report success with failing or unrun tests, and never delete, skip, or weaken a test to make it pass.

## ML-specific guidance

Model training is slow; e2e tests must still be real but can be small: tiny configs (e.g., 2-layer, 64-dim), tiny fixture corpora committed under `tests/fixtures/`, a handful of steps. Assert on real observable behavior — loss decreases over N steps, checkpoint round-trips, tokenizer encode/decode is identity — not on screenshots of internals. Seed all randomness inside tests so failures reproduce.

- `vocab: dict[bytes, int]` — trained BPE merges mapping byte pairs to token ids. Must contain the 256 base byte tokens.
- `max_tokens: int | None` — truncate output after this many tokens; `None` (default) means no truncation. Must be positive when given.

**Returns:** `list[int]` of token ids in document order. Empty list only when `max_tokens=0` is impossible by constraint, so an empty return never occurs; a missing/empty corpus raises instead.

**Side effects:** None. Pure function; reads `corpus_path` but writes nothing.

**Raises:**
- `FileNotFoundError` — `corpus_path` does not exist.
- `ValueError` — corpus file is empty, or `max_tokens` is zero/negative, with the offending value in the message.

**Callers/Callees:** Called by `build_training_batches` (src/train/batch.py). Calls `merge_byte_pairs` (src/data/tokenizer.py).

**Last modified:** 2026-06-09 — added max_tokens truncation for memory-bounded training runs.
```

## Pruning

Quick prune at the end of every response: grep the names of functions you touched, delete entries whose function is gone. Full audit of every entry — existence, path, callers — only on explicit user request. Never delete source code under this procedure.

# Process Procedures: Scope, Commits, Dependencies, Config

## Scope discipline

Touch only the files and lines the task requires.

- Editing one file is never license to refactor, reformat, rename, or delete anything in another.
- Before editing a function, check its Callers/Callees in `docs/functions.md` to know what depends on it; after editing, `make test` proves dependents still work.
- After the task, review `git diff` line by line. Every changed line must be justified by the task; revert anything that is not.
- Out-of-scope problems you discover (a bug elsewhere, dead code in another file, an unpinned dependency you didn't introduce) are journal findings. If one genuinely blocks the task, journal it and ask the user before touching it.

## Commits

- Commit after every small unit of work that leaves the repo in a working state: a function added, a bug fixed, a test passing, a doc entry written. Many small commits per session; one big end-of-session commit is a violation.
- Committing is the default, not something to ask permission for. Never end a session with verified work sitting uncommitted. (Pushing and anything history-rewriting still require the user.)
- Messages: one line, lowercase, plain words stating what changed. No Conventional Commits prefixes, no bullet lists, no bodies, no co-author trailers, no emoji.

```
fix off-by-one in batch loader
pin numpy to 2.3.4
add proving test for bpe merge order
```

- Never commit a known-broken state silently. If you must checkpoint broken work, mark it (`wip: parser broken on empty input`) and fix it in the immediately following commits.
- One logical change per commit. Frequent commits are what makes "git history is the archive" true for deleted code.

## Dependencies

- Exact pins only in `requirements.txt`: `torch==2.9.1`. Never `>=`, `~=`, `^`, or bare names.
- Adding a dependency: prove the usage in `tests/` first (sandbox rule), pin the exact version you tested against, update `make setup` if needed, journal why the dependency was necessary.
- Prefer the standard library when it does the job adequately; every dependency is future breakage risk.
- Never upgrade a dependency as a side effect of another task. Upgrades are their own explicit task with full test verification.
- If you find an unpinned entry while already working in `requirements.txt`, pin it to the installed version and journal it.

## Configuration and secrets

- No secrets in code or git, ever: keys, tokens, passwords come from environment variables or a git-ignored `.env`. A needed-but-missing secret means stop and ask the user.
- No absolute paths in code; compute paths relative to the repository root.
- All tunable values (paths, ports, hyperparameters, thresholds) live in one config module, not as magic literals scattered across files. Defaults must be sane enough that `make run` and `make test` work with zero manual configuration.
- Document each config value's meaning and default in `docs/functions.md` alongside the config module's entry.

## Makefile contract

`make setup`, `make test`, `make lint`, `make fix`, and `make run` must always work argument-free. Any change to how the project installs, runs, lints, or tests is incomplete until the corresponding target is updated and re-run successfully in the same session. `make setup` must be idempotent: a second consecutive run succeeds and changes nothing.

import math
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from src.mythosmini.leaderboard.entries import (
    LeaderboardEntry,
    parse_leaderboard_html,
    parse_params_text,
)
from src.mythosmini.leaderboard.placement import compute_placement, format_placement, rank_of
from src.mythosmini.leaderboard.scoring import (
    build_wiki_normalization,
    efficiency_score,
    overall_score,
    wiki_score,
)

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures" / "leaderboard_index.html"


def load_entries() -> list[LeaderboardEntry]:
    return parse_leaderboard_html(FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def test_parse_params_text_handles_suffixes() -> None:
    assert parse_params_text("1M") == 1e6
    assert parse_params_text("587K") == 587e3
    assert parse_params_text("1.71M") == 1.71e6
    assert parse_params_text("2B") == 2e9
    assert parse_params_text("1234") == 1234.0


def test_parse_params_text_rejects_empty() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        parse_params_text("")


def test_parse_leaderboard_html_finds_known_entries() -> None:
    entries = load_entries()
    assert len(entries) >= 20
    by_name = {entry.name: entry for entry in entries}
    glint = by_name["Glint-0.1"]
    assert glint.params == 1e6
    assert glint.blimp == 46.7
    assert glint.arc == 21.0
    assert glint.wiki is None
    cinnabar = by_name["CinnabarLM 1.4M"]
    assert cinnabar.wiki == 2.316
    assert cinnabar.params == 1.51e6


def test_overall_score_without_wiki_matches_site_formula() -> None:
    entries = load_entries()
    norm = build_wiki_normalization(entries)
    glint = next(entry for entry in entries if entry.name == "Glint-0.1")
    assert overall_score(glint, norm) == pytest.approx((46.7 + 21.0 + 0.0) / 3.0)


def test_wiki_score_normalization_bounds() -> None:
    entries = load_entries()
    norm = build_wiki_normalization(entries)
    wikis = [entry.wiki for entry in entries if entry.wiki is not None and entry.wiki > 0]
    best_entry = next(entry for entry in entries if entry.wiki == min(wikis))
    worst_capped = next(entry for entry in entries if entry.wiki == max(wikis))
    best = wiki_score(best_entry, norm)
    worst = wiki_score(worst_capped, norm)
    assert best == pytest.approx(100.0)
    assert worst == pytest.approx(0.0)


def test_efficiency_score_divides_by_log_params() -> None:
    entries = load_entries()
    norm = build_wiki_normalization(entries)
    glint = next(entry for entry in entries if entry.name == "Glint-0.1")
    expected = overall_score(glint, norm) / math.log10(1e6 + 1.0)
    assert efficiency_score(glint, norm) == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_rank_of_counts_strictly_better() -> None:
    assert rank_of(5.0, [9.0, 7.0, 3.0]) == 3
    assert rank_of(10.0, [9.0, 7.0, 3.0]) == 1
    assert rank_of(1.0, []) == 1


def test_compute_placement_inserts_candidate() -> None:
    entries = load_entries()
    candidate = LeaderboardEntry(
        name="MythosMini", params=1.05e6, blimp=99.0, arc=99.0, wiki=1.01
    )
    placement = compute_placement(candidate, entries)
    assert placement.total_entries == len(entries) + 1
    assert placement.overall_rank == 1
    assert placement.efficiency_rank == 1
    text = format_placement("checkpoint 2000", placement)
    assert "rank 1/" in text
    assert "overall" in text and "efficiency" in text


def test_compute_placement_bottom_candidate() -> None:
    entries = load_entries()
    candidate = LeaderboardEntry(
        name="MythosMini", params=1.05e6, blimp=0.1, arc=0.1, wiki=499.0
    )
    placement = compute_placement(candidate, entries)
    assert placement.overall_rank > 1
    assert placement.overall >= 0.0

from src.mythosmini.hardware.autotune import (

def test_detect_device_returns_consistent_info() -> None:
    info = detect_device()
    assert info.device in ("cuda", "cpu")
    assert info.cpu_threads >= 1
    assert describe_device(info)
    if info.device == "cuda":
        assert info.free_memory_bytes > 0
        assert refresh_free_memory(info) > 0
    else:
        assert refresh_free_memory(info) == 0


def test_autocast_dtype_matches_capability() -> None:
    info = detect_device()
    dtype = autocast_dtype(info)
    if info.device == "cuda" and info.supports_bf16:
        assert dtype == torch.bfloat16
    else:
        assert dtype == torch.float32


def test_shrink_after_oom_decrements_by_five_and_compensates() -> None:
    plan = BatchPlan(micro_batch=64, grad_accum=1)
    shrunk = shrink_after_oom(plan)
    assert shrunk.micro_batch == 59
    assert shrunk.grad_accum == 2
    assert shrunk.effective_batch >= plan.effective_batch


def test_shrink_after_oom_never_drops_below_one() -> None:

    shrunk = shrink_after_oom(plan)

    assert shrunk.effective_batch >= 12

    def exploding_step(batch_size: int) -> None:
        raise torch.OutOfMemoryError("simulated out of memory")

    assert probe_throughput(exploding_step, 8, 512, "cpu") is None


def test_autotune_batch_size_picks_fastest_real_step() -> None:
    info = detect_device()
    weights = torch.randn(64, 64, device=info.device)

    def real_step(batch_size: int) -> None:
        data = torch.randn(batch_size, 64, device=info.device)
        (data @ weights).sum().backward() if False else (data @ weights).sum().item()

    plan = autotune_batch_size(real_step, seq_len=64, info=info)
    assert plan.micro_batch >= 1
    assert plan.grad_accum == 1

import torch

from src.mythosmini.config import ModelConfig
from src.mythosmini.model.transformer import MythosMini, build_rope_cache, count_parameters


def tiny_config() -> ModelConfig:
    return ModelConfig(
        dim=32,
        n_heads=2,
        prelude_layers=1,
        coda_layers=1,
        shared_loops=2,
        lora_rank=2,
        ffn_hidden=64,
        max_seq_len=64,
    )


def test_default_config_lands_near_one_million_parameters() -> None:
    model = MythosMini(ModelConfig())
    total = count_parameters(model)
    assert 950_000 <= total <= 1_150_000


def test_forward_shape_and_finite_logits() -> None:
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    model = MythosMini(tiny_config())
    tokens = torch.randint(0, 257, (2, 16))
    logits = model(tokens)
    assert logits.shape == (2, 16, 257)
    assert torch.isfinite(logits).all()


def test_variable_loop_counts_change_output() -> None:
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    model = MythosMini(tiny_config())
    model.eval()
    tokens = torch.randint(0, 257, (1, 16))
    with torch.no_grad():
        for parameter in model.loop_lora.up:
            torch.nn.init.normal_(parameter.weight, std=0.1)
        one = model(tokens, loops=1)
        four = model(tokens, loops=4)
    assert not torch.allclose(one, four)


def test_rope_cache_shapes() -> None:
    config = tiny_config()
    cos, sin = build_rope_cache(config)
    assert cos.shape == (64, 8)
    assert sin.shape == (64, 8)


def test_loss_decreases_over_training_steps() -> None:
    torch.manual_seed(7)
    model = MythosMini(tiny_config())
    tokens = torch.randint(0, 257, (4, 32))
    optimizer = torch.optim.NAdam(model.parameters(), lr=3e-3, decoupled_weight_decay=True)
    losses: list[float] = []
    for _ in range(30):
        logits = model(tokens[:, :-1])
        loss = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(
            logits.reshape(-1, 257), tokens[:, 1:].reshape(-1)
        )
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        losses.append(loss.item())
    assert losses[-1] < losses[0] * 0.8

        self.out = nn.Linear(config.dim, config.dim, bias=False)

        batch, seq_len, dim = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x)

        q, k, v = qkv.split(dim, dim=-1)

import torch
from src.mythosmini.config import ModelConfig
from src.mythosmini.model.transformer import MythosMini, build_rope_cache, count_parameters


def tiny_config() -> ModelConfig:
    return ModelConfig(
        dim=32,
        n_heads=2,
        prelude_layers=1,
        coda_layers=1,
        shared_loops=2,
        lora_rank=2,
        ffn_hidden=64,
        max_seq_len=64,
    )


def test_default_config_lands_near_one_million_parameters() -> None:
    model = MythosMini(ModelConfig())
    total = count_parameters(model)
    assert 950_000 <= total <= 1_150_000


def test_forward_shape_and_finite_logits() -> None:
    torch.manual_seed(0)

import pytest
import torch

from src.mythosmini.config import EOS_TOKEN_ID
from src.mythosmini.data.buffer import SequenceBuffer
from src.mythosmini.data.packing import byte_tokenize, pack_token_stream, quality_passes


def test_byte_tokenize_round_trip_with_eos() -> None:
    tokens = byte_tokenize("hello")
    assert tokens == [104, 101, 108, 108, 111, EOS_TOKEN_ID]
    assert bytes(tokens[:-1]).decode("utf-8") == "hello"


def test_byte_tokenize_handles_multibyte_utf8() -> None:
    tokens = byte_tokenize("héllo")
    assert tokens[-1] == EOS_TOKEN_ID
    assert bytes(tokens[:-1]).decode("utf-8") == "héllo"
    assert all(0 <= token <= 256 for token in tokens)


def test_pack_token_stream_yields_fixed_blocks() -> None:
    documents = iter(["a" * 100, "b" * 100, "c" * 100])
    blocks = list(pack_token_stream(documents, seq_len=64))
    assert len(blocks) == 4
    for block in blocks:
        assert block.shape == (65,)
        assert block.dtype == torch.long


def test_pack_token_stream_preserves_document_order() -> None:
    documents = iter(["ab", "cd"])
    blocks = list(pack_token_stream(documents, seq_len=2))
    flat = torch.cat(blocks).tolist()
    assert flat[:3] == [ord("a"), ord("b"), EOS_TOKEN_ID]


def test_pack_token_stream_rejects_tiny_seq_len() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        list(pack_token_stream(iter(["abc"]), seq_len=1))


def test_quality_passes_keeps_score_at_or_above_threshold() -> None:
    assert quality_passes(4, 4)
    assert quality_passes(5, 4)
    assert not quality_passes(3, 4)


def test_sequence_buffer_slices_arbitrary_batch_sizes() -> None:
    chunks = iter([torch.arange(12).reshape(4, 3), torch.arange(12, 24).reshape(4, 3)])
    buffer = SequenceBuffer(chunks, device="cpu")
    first = buffer.next_batch(3)
    second = buffer.next_batch(5)
    assert first is not None and first.shape == (3, 3)
    assert second is not None and second.shape == (5, 3)
    assert first[0].tolist() == [0, 1, 2]
    assert second[-1].tolist() == [21, 22, 23]
    assert buffer.next_batch(1) is None


def test_sequence_buffer_rejects_nonpositive_batch() -> None:
    buffer = SequenceBuffer(iter([]), device="cpu")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        buffer.next_batch(0)

def test_required_files_exist() -> None:
    missing = [name for name in REQUIRED_FILES if not (REPO_ROOT / name).is_file()]

    assert entries != [], "requirements.txt is empty"
    unpinned = [entry for entry in entries if not EXACT_PIN_PATTERN.match(entry)]
    assert unpinned == [], f"dependencies not exactly pinned: {unpinned}"


def test_makefile_defines_required_targets() -> None:
    makefile = (REPO_ROOT / "Makefile").read_text()
    missing = [
        target for target in ("setup:", "test:", "lint:", "fix:", "run:") if target not in makefile
    ]
    assert missing == [], f"Makefile targets missing: {missing}"


def test_source_files_contain_no_comments() -> None:
    offenders: list[str] = []
    for source_file in (REPO_ROOT / "src").rglob("*.py"):
        for line_number, line in enumerate(source_file.read_text().splitlines(), start=1):
            if line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
                offenders.append(f"{source_file.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}:{line_number}")
    assert offenders == [], f"comments found in source files: {offenders}"

from src.mythosmini.config import TrainConfig


def lr_at_step(step: int, total_steps: int, config: TrainConfig) -> float:
    if total_steps < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"total_steps must be positive, got {total_steps}")
    warmup_steps = max(1, int(total_steps * config.warmup_fraction))
    decay_steps = max(1, int(total_steps * config.decay_fraction))
    decay_start = total_steps - decay_steps
    floor = config.peak_lr * config.min_lr_fraction
    if step < warmup_steps:
        return config.peak_lr * (step + 1) / warmup_steps
    if step < decay_start:
        return config.peak_lr
    progress = min(1.0, (step - decay_start) / decay_steps)
    return config.peak_lr + (floor - config.peak_lr) * progress

import json
import queue
import threading
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


class RunLog:
    def __init__(self, log_path: Path) -> None:
        self.log_path = log_path
        self.entries: queue.Queue[dict[str, Any] | None] = queue.Queue()
        self.worker = threading.Thread(target=self.drain, daemon=True)
        self.worker.start()

    def drain(self) -> None:
        self.log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self.log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            while True:
                entry = self.entries.get()
                if entry is None:
                    self.entries.task_done()
                    return
                handle.write(json.dumps(entry) + "\n")
                handle.flush()
                self.entries.task_done()

    def log(self, entry: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.entries.put(entry)

    def shutdown(self) -> None:
        self.entries.put(None)
        self.worker.join()

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import torch

import src.mythosmini.training.loop as loop_module
from src.mythosmini.checkpointing.saver import BackgroundSaver, cpu_clone_state
from src.mythosmini.config import ModelConfig, TrainConfig
from src.mythosmini.data.buffer import SequenceBuffer
from src.mythosmini.hardware.autotune import BatchPlan
from src.mythosmini.hardware.detect import DeviceInfo
from src.mythosmini.model.transformer import MythosMini
from src.mythosmini.telemetry.progress import build_progress_bar
from src.mythosmini.telemetry.runlog import RunLog
from src.mythosmini.training.loop import TrainerDeps, TrainState, run_training
from src.mythosmini.training.optimizer import build_nadamw
from src.mythosmini.training.scheduler import lr_at_step


def cpu_device_info() -> DeviceInfo:
    return DeviceInfo(
        device="cpu",
        name="cpu",
        total_memory_bytes=0,
        free_memory_bytes=0,
        supports_bf16=False,
        cpu_threads=1,
    )


def tiny_model_config() -> ModelConfig:
    return ModelConfig(
        dim=32,
        n_heads=2,
        prelude_layers=1,
        coda_layers=1,
        shared_loops=2,
        lora_rank=2,
        ffn_hidden=64,
        max_seq_len=64,
    )


def test_lr_schedule_has_warmup_stable_decay() -> None:
    config = TrainConfig(token_budget=0, peak_lr=1.0, warmup_fraction=0.1, decay_fraction=0.2)
    assert lr_at_step(0, 100, config) == pytest.approx(0.1)
    assert lr_at_step(9, 100, config) == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert lr_at_step(50, 100, config) == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert lr_at_step(99, 100, config) < 0.2
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        lr_at_step(0, 0, config)


def test_background_saver_atomic_round_trip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    saver = BackgroundSaver()
    payload = {"weights": torch.arange(4, dtype=torch.float32), "step": 7}
    destination = tmp_path / "checkpoints" / "step_00000007.pt"
    saver.submit(payload, destination)
    saver.wait_for_all()
    saver.shutdown()
    assert destination.is_file()
    assert not destination.with_suffix(".tmp").exists()
    loaded = torch.load(destination)
    assert loaded["step"] == 7
    assert torch.equal(loaded["weights"], payload["weights"])


def test_cpu_clone_state_detaches_nested_tensors() -> None:
    source = {"a": torch.ones(2, requires_grad=True), "b": {"c": torch.zeros(3)}, "d": 5}
    cloned = cpu_clone_state(source)
    assert not cloned["a"].requires_grad
    assert torch.equal(cloned["b"]["c"], torch.zeros(3))
    assert cloned["d"] == 5


def test_runlog_writes_json_lines(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    log_path = tmp_path / "logs" / "run.jsonl"
    run_log = RunLog(log_path)
    run_log.log({"step": 1, "loss": 2.5})
    run_log.log({"step": 2, "loss": 2.4})
    run_log.shutdown()
    lines = log_path.read_text().splitlines()
    assert len(lines) == 2
    assert json.loads(lines[0]) == {"step": 1, "loss": 2.5}


def synthetic_chunks(count: int, rows: int, seq_len: int) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(11)

    }
    deps.saver.submit(payload, destination)
    state.saved_checkpoints.append(destination)
    return destination


def log_progress(deps: TrainerDeps, state: TrainState, lr: float, saved: Path | None) -> None:
    message = (
        f"step {state.step} tokens {state.tokens_done} loss {state.last_loss:.4f} "
        f"lr {lr:.2e} micro_batch {state.plan.micro_batch} accum {state.plan.grad_accum}"
    )
    if saved is not None:
        message += f" checkpoint {saved.name}"
    emit_log_line(deps.bar, message)
    deps.run_log.log(
        {
            "step": state.step,
            "tokens": state.tokens_done,
            "loss": state.last_loss,
            "lr": lr,
            "micro_batch": state.plan.micro_batch,
            "grad_accum": state.plan.grad_accum,
            "checkpoint": saved.name if saved is not None else None,
        }
    )


def run_training(deps: TrainerDeps, initial_plan: BatchPlan, token_budget: int) -> TrainState:
    config = deps.train_config
    state = TrainState(plan=initial_plan)
    optimizer = build_nadamw(deps.model, config)
    dtype = autocast_dtype(deps.device_info)
    rng = random.Random(config.seed)
    tokens_per_step = initial_plan.effective_batch * config.seq_len
    total_steps = max(1, token_budget // tokens_per_step)
    deps.model.train()
    latest_loss: Tensor | None = None
    while state.tokens_done < token_budget:
        lr = lr_at_step(state.step, total_steps, config)
        for group in optimizer.param_groups:
            group["lr"] = lr
        loops = rng.randint(config.loop_min, config.loop_max)
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        mean_loss = accumulate_gradients(deps, state, loops, dtype)
        if mean_loss is None:
            emit_log_line(deps.bar, f"data stream exhausted at step {state.step}")
            break
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(deps.model.parameters(), config.grad_clip)
        optimizer.step()
        latest_loss = mean_loss
        state.step += 1
        step_tokens = state.plan.effective_batch * config.seq_len
        state.tokens_done += step_tokens
        deps.bar.update(step_tokens)
        should_checkpoint = state.step % CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_STEPS == 0
        if should_checkpoint or state.step % LOG_INTERVAL_STEPS == 0:
            state.last_loss = float(mean_loss.item())
            saved = save_checkpoint(deps, state, optimizer) if should_checkpoint else None
            log_progress(deps, state, lr, saved)
    already_saved = state.step % CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_STEPS == 0 and state.saved_checkpoints
    if not already_saved:
        final = save_checkpoint(deps, state, optimizer)
        log_progress(deps, state, lr_at_step(state.step, total_steps, config), final)
    deps.saver.wait_for_all()
    return state

    failures = {"remaining": 2}

    def flaky_compute(
        model: MythosMini, batch: torch.Tensor, loops: int, dtype: torch.dtype
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        if failures["remaining"] > 0:

            raise torch.OutOfMemoryError("simulated oom")

    deps.run_log.shutdown()
    deps.saver.shutdown()
    assert state.plan.micro_batch == 1
    assert state.plan.grad_accum == 9
    assert state.step >= 4

    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        if failures["remaining"] > 0:
            failures["remaining"] -= 1
            raise torch.OutOfMemoryError("simulated oom")
        return real_compute(model, batch, loops, dtype)

    monkeypatch.setattr(loop_module, "compute_loss", flaky_compute)
    state = run_training(deps, BatchPlan(micro_batch=8, grad_accum=1), token_budget=5 * 8 * 32)
    deps.bar.close()
    deps.run_log.shutdown()
    deps.saver.shutdown()
    assert state.plan.micro_batch == 1
    assert state.plan.grad_accum == 9
    assert state.step >= 4

from dataclasses import dataclass

import torch
from torch import Tensor
from torch.nn import functional

from src.mythosmini.model.transformer import MythosMini


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScoredPair:
    context: list[int]
    continuation: list[int]


def truncate_pair(pair: ScoredPair, max_len: int) -> tuple[list[int], int]:
    if not pair.continuation:
        raise ValueError("continuation must contain at least one token")
    full = pair.context + pair.continuation
    kept = full[-max_len:]
    continuation_len = min(len(pair.continuation), max_len - 1)
    return kept, continuation_len


def batch_log_likelihoods(
    model: MythosMini, rows: list[tuple[list[int], int]], device: str, dtype: torch.dtype
) -> list[float]:
    max_len = max(len(tokens) for tokens, _ in rows)
    padded = torch.zeros(len(rows), max_len, dtype=torch.long)
    for index, (tokens, _) in enumerate(rows):
        padded[index, : len(tokens)] = torch.tensor(tokens, dtype=torch.long)
    batch = padded.to(device)
    with torch.autocast(device_type=device, dtype=dtype, enabled=dtype != torch.float32):
        logits = model(batch[:, :-1])
    log_probs = functional.log_softmax(logits.float(), dim=-1)
    target_scores = log_probs.gather(-1, batch[:, 1:].unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
    results: list[float] = []
    for index, (tokens, continuation_len) in enumerate(rows):
        end = len(tokens) - 1
        start = end - continuation_len
        results.append(float(target_scores[index, start:end].sum().item()))
    return results


def continuation_log_likelihoods(
    model: MythosMini,
    pairs: list[ScoredPair],
    batch_size: int,
    device: str,
    dtype: torch.dtype,
) -> list[float]:
    if batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"batch_size must be positive, got {batch_size}")
    max_len = model.config.max_seq_len
    rows = [truncate_pair(pair, max_len) for pair in pairs]
    order = sorted(range(len(rows)), key=lambda index: len(rows[index][0]), reverse=True)
    results = [0.0] * len(rows)
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for chunk_start in range(0, len(order), batch_size):
            chunk = order[chunk_start : chunk_start + batch_size]
            chunk_rows = [rows[index] for index in chunk]
            scores = batch_log_likelihoods(model, chunk_rows, device, dtype)
            for index, score in zip(chunk, scores, strict=True):
                results[index] = score
    return results

import math

import torch
from torch.nn import functional

from src.mythosmini.config import WIKITEXT_CONFIG, WIKITEXT_DATASET, WIKITEXT_MAX_BYTES
from src.mythosmini.model.transformer import MythosMini


def load_wikitext_bytes(max_bytes: int = WIKITEXT_MAX_BYTES) -> bytes:
    from datasets import load_dataset

    dataset = load_dataset(WIKITEXT_DATASET, name=WIKITEXT_CONFIG, split="test")
    joined = "".join(str(record["text"]) for record in dataset)
    return joined.encode("utf-8")[:max_bytes]


def byte_perplexity(
    model: MythosMini, raw_bytes: bytes, batch_size: int, device: str, dtype: torch.dtype
) -> float:
    if not raw_bytes:
        raise ValueError("wikitext byte stream is empty")
    seq_len = model.config.max_seq_len
    tokens = torch.tensor(list(raw_bytes), dtype=torch.long)
    usable = (len(tokens) - 1) // seq_len * seq_len
    if usable == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"need more than {seq_len} bytes, got {len(raw_bytes)}")
    inputs = tokens[:usable].reshape(-1, seq_len)
    targets = tokens[1 : usable + 1].reshape(-1, seq_len)
    total_nll = 0.0
    total_count = 0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for start in range(0, inputs.shape[0], batch_size):
            batch = inputs[start : start + batch_size].to(device)
            target = targets[start : start + batch_size].to(device)
            with torch.autocast(device_type=device, dtype=dtype, enabled=dtype != torch.float32):
                logits = model(batch)
            nll = functional.cross_entropy(
                logits.float().reshape(-1, logits.shape[-1]), target.reshape(-1), reduction="sum"
            )
            total_nll += float(nll.item())
            total_count += int(target.numel())
    return math.exp(total_nll / total_count)

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from src.mythosmini.benchmarks.arc import ArcQuestion, arc_accuracy, load_arc_questions
from src.mythosmini.benchmarks.blimp import blimp_accuracy, load_blimp_pairs
from src.mythosmini.benchmarks.wikitext import byte_perplexity, load_wikitext_bytes
from src.mythosmini.config import ModelConfig
from src.mythosmini.hardware.autotune import autotune_batch_size
from src.mythosmini.hardware.detect import DeviceInfo, autocast_dtype
from src.mythosmini.leaderboard.entries import LeaderboardEntry
from src.mythosmini.model.transformer import MythosMini, count_parameters


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BenchmarkData:
    wikitext_bytes: bytes
    blimp_subtasks: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]]
    arc_prefix: str
    arc_questions: list[ArcQuestion]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BenchmarkScores:
    wiki_ppl: float
    blimp: float
    arc: float


def load_benchmark_data() -> BenchmarkData:
    prefix, questions = load_arc_questions()
    return BenchmarkData(
        wikitext_bytes=load_wikitext_bytes(),
        blimp_subtasks=load_blimp_pairs(),
        arc_prefix=prefix,
        arc_questions=questions,
    )


def load_model_from_checkpoint(path: Path, device: str) -> MythosMini:
    checkpoint = torch.load(path, map_location=device)
    config = ModelConfig(**checkpoint["model_config"])
    model = MythosMini(config)
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model"])
    model.to(device)
    model.eval()
    return model


def autotune_eval_batch(model: MythosMini, info: DeviceInfo) -> int:
    seq_len = model.config.max_seq_len
    dtype = autocast_dtype(info)

    def forward_step(batch_size: int) -> None:
        tokens = torch.randint(0, model.config.vocab_size, (batch_size, seq_len), device=info.device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            with torch.autocast(
                device_type=info.device, dtype=dtype, enabled=dtype != torch.float32
            ):
                model(tokens)

    plan = autotune_batch_size(forward_step, seq_len, info)
    return plan.micro_batch


def benchmark_model(
    model: MythosMini, data: BenchmarkData, batch_size: int, info: DeviceInfo
) -> BenchmarkScores:
    dtype = autocast_dtype(info)
    return BenchmarkScores(
        wiki_ppl=byte_perplexity(model, data.wikitext_bytes, batch_size, info.device, dtype),
        blimp=blimp_accuracy(model, data.blimp_subtasks, batch_size, info.device, dtype),
        arc=arc_accuracy(
            model, data.arc_prefix, data.arc_questions, batch_size, info.device, dtype
        ),
    )


def scores_to_entry(name: str, parameter_count: int, scores: BenchmarkScores) -> LeaderboardEntry:
    return LeaderboardEntry(
        name=name,
        params=float(parameter_count),
        blimp=scores.blimp,
        arc=scores.arc,
        wiki=scores.wiki_ppl,
    )


def model_entry_params(model: MythosMini) -> int:
    return count_parameters(model)
